Hardware

ESP32-S3 board

Any ESP32-S3 board with 8 MB octal PSRAM and at least 8 MB of quad flash (N16R8 or N8R8 modules). It has two USB-C ports: COM, through a USB-to-serial chip, and USB, the chip's own USB. Either port powers the board and can flash it; while a USB device is active, flash and read logs through COM.

Tested with: ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 N16R8 (affiliate link).

Supported boards

5 V USB charger (required)

The board always needs a 5 V supply. Without a USB device, plug the charger straight into either port, COM or USB. With a USB device, put the charger on the Y-cable's power input instead: one charger of at least 2.5 A powers both the board and the device, with nothing on the COM port. Keep it independent of the NAS or PC the gateway should wake.

Powering USB devices

Wi-Fi, built in

The built-in 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi connects to your router and, if you want, also runs the gateway's own access point for IoT devices. Both share one radio and one channel.

Network modes

Computer on the COM port (optional)

Use the COM port to flash the firmware (browser installer, Easy Install) and to read the logs. Day to day it is not needed: updates arrive over the air from System → Updates. While a USB device is active, flash and read logs through COM, not through USB.

Install the firmware

microSD (optional)

An optional microSD card (SDMMC 1-bit on GPIO38/39/40) keeps a flight recorder of the logs. The firmware runs without it.

Pins and wiring

W5500 Ethernet on the pins (optional) Not yet tested

A W5500 SPI module, or an ESP32-S3 board with built-in Ethernet and PoE. The driver is in the standard image, off until configured, Wi-Fi-first or Ethernet-first. Ethernet can also use a USB adapter on the USB port. Experimental: not yet validated on real hardware.

Ethernet guide

4G modem with a SIM on the pins (optional) Not yet tested

A 4G/LTE modem module wired to UART pins, with its own 5 V supply for 2 A peaks, as the main or backup uplink. A SIM can also use a USB stick or modem on the USB port. Not yet tested with a real modem.

Cellular guide

OTG Y-cable with power input (optional)

Needed only for a USB device (4G stick, USB modem, USB Ethernet or a phone). Its USB-C plug goes into the board's USB port (data and 5 V), the device into its USB-A socket, the charger into its power input. It must pass data: charge-only splitters do not work. The board does not supply 5 V on its USB port by itself.

Y-cable guide

4G USB stick or modem with a SIM (optional)

A 4G/LTE USB stick or USB modem with a SIM on the USB port, as the main or backup Internet uplink, with failover and an optional monthly data limit: Tailscale runs over mobile data and name lookups go over the SIM. A modem can also be wired to the pins instead (UART).

Tested with: TCL LinkKey IK41 (affiliate link).

USB devices

USB Ethernet adapter or phone tethering (optional) Not yet tested

A USB Ethernet adapter (Realtek RTL8152/8153/8156, CDC-ECM/NCM) or Android USB tethering on the USB port, as the main or backup uplink. Ethernet can also use a W5500 module on the pins (SPI). Not yet tested with real devices.

USB devices

The firmware runs on an ESP32-S3 with 8 MB octal PSRAM and at least 8 MB of quad flash: N8R8 and N16R8 modules. One image serves both; a 16 MB board uses the first 8 MB.

Buy the tested board

The gateway is developed and tested on the ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 N16R8 (16 MB flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM). If you do not have a board yet, these are the ones used for development:

ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 N16R8 on Amazon (1) ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 N16R8 on Amazon (2)

For a wired connection: an ESP32-S3 board with built-in Ethernet and a PoE module. ESP32-S3 with Ethernet and PoE on Amazon

Ethernet support (W5500) is experimental and not yet validated on real hardware; check that the board has 8 MB octal PSRAM (R8) and at least 8 MB of flash, and set its W5500 pins under Network → Ethernet.

Supported ESP32-S3 boards

BoardFlash · PSRAMStatus
ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 N16R8, ESP32-S3-WROOM-1/1U-N16R816 MB quad · 8 MB octalTested (reference board)
ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 N8R8, ESP32-S3-WROOM-1/1U-N8R88 MB quad · 8 MB octalSame flash layout; hardware validation pending
Freenove ESP32-S3-WROOM N8R8 / N16R88–16 MB · 8 MB octalSupported; community-confirmed on earlier firmware
Seeed XIAO ESP32S3 (8 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM)8 MB · 8 MB octalSupported; community-confirmed on earlier firmware

The module marking tells you the variant: N is the flash and R the PSRAM in MB. You need N8 or more and R8.

Not supported

  • 4 MB flash (N4, N4R2, N4R8): The current firmware requires at least 8 MB of flash.
  • 2 MB quad PSRAM or no PSRAM (N8R2, N16R2, N8, N16): the image expects 8 MB octal PSRAM.
  • Octal-flash modules (ESP32-S3-WROOM-2, N16R16V, N32R8V, N32R16V): the image uses quad flash.
  • Other chips (ESP32, ESP32-S2, C3, C5, C6, H2, P4): the installers refuse anything that is not an ESP32-S3.
  • YD-ESP32-S3 clones: reported not working (access point not visible, a board-level RF issue).

Requirements

SoCESP32-S3 (dual core, 2.4 GHz WiFi)
MemoryAt least 8 MB quad flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM (N8R8 or N16R8)
PowerReliable USB supply, separate from the machines it should wake
OptionalmicroSD card for the log flight recorder

Community reports for other ESP32-S3 boards are collected in docs/HARDWARE.md; please add yours with the Hardware report issue form.

Cellular (SIM) and W5500 Ethernet

Tested 4G USB stick: a TCL LinkKey IK41 with a SIM, as the main Internet uplink with Tailscale connected over mobile data. TCL LinkKey IK41 4G USB stick on Amazon

Affiliate link: buying through it supports the project at no extra cost to you. As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.

From 3.0.25 a USB LTE modem, a 4G stick, a USB Ethernet adapter or phone tethering can also use the board's USB port. The board does not power that port: read USB modems, sticks and Ethernet adapters before plugging anything in.

The standard firmware image includes a driver for an explicitly wired W5500 SPI module: off until configured, explicit pins, DHCP or static IPv4, WiFi-first or Ethernet-first. It is host-tested only and not validated on real hardware; wire it as documented in docs/ETHERNET.md, or use an ESP32-S3 board with built-in Ethernet and PoE (see above). A UART cellular modem with a SIM can also be used as a primary or failover uplink, off until configured; UART modems are not yet tested with real hardware (docs/CELLULAR.md).

Single radio

The uplink and the access point share one 2.4 GHz radio and channel. After a roam to a different channel the device realigns the AP, which briefly interrupts AP clients.
